Here's what was going on with the login redirects. The session cookie was set with SameSite=Strict, so the browser didn't send it when the identity provider redirected back. Why did it only break on Safari? Because Chrome was still giving top-level POSTs a lax-by-default grace period. I changed it to SameSite=Lax, which is the standard setting for OAuth callbacks. I verified the full flow in Safari, Chrome and Firefox. The fix is merged and deployed to production.

The off-by-one-day bug in the invoice dates came from naive datetimes. The service parsed timestamps without a timezone and then compared them with UTC values from Postgres. Why did it only show up for Australian customers? Because their local midnight is still the previous day in UTC. I made every parse timezone-aware and normalized to UTC at the boundary. The regression test covers Sydney, Honolulu and London. It's deployed.

I rewrote the WebSocket reconnect logic in the React Native app. The old code retried immediately in a tight loop, which drained the battery and got throttled by the server. I added unit tests for the backoff schedule. Did the WebSocket reconnect work after you toggled airplane mode?
